sections.skill: Build a startup budget with assumptions and contingency

questions.prompt: What is a contingency in a budget?

choices.text: Money owed to customers for refunds
Extra money set aside for surprises
A tax paid to the state each month
The owner's profit for the first year

questions.correct_answer: Extra money set aside for surprises
questions.intro: A STARTUP BUDGET lists what you expect to spend before and during the first months. List one-time costs (equipment, filing fees, first inventory) and recurring costs for several months, because sales often start slowly. Add a CONTINGENCY: an extra amount, often a percentage, for surprises such as a repair or a price increase. Write down your ASSUMPTIONS (for example, "rent stays 400 dollars a month") so you can check them later. Compare the total with the money available.

questions.prompt: Why include several months of recurring costs?

choices.text: It makes the budget look smaller
Banks require exactly twelve months listed
Recurring costs are paid only once

sections.skill: Finding a percent of an amount

questions.prompt: What is 10 percent of 500?
questions.intro: To find a percent of an amount, change the percent to a decimal and multiply. 10 percent = 0.10, 15 percent = 0.15, 5 percent = 0.05. Example: 10 percent of 3,000 is 0.10 x 3,000 = 300. To ADD a percent, multiply by 1 plus the decimal: 3,000 x 1.10 = 3,300. Check: 10 percent is one tenth, so move the decimal point one place.
